q-80398.name: Question 1
q-80398.problem: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x}$ given that $\frac{∂f}{∂x}={y}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{2}+2y}.$
q-80398.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{∂f}{∂x}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{2}+2y}) \\  & =2y{e}^{{x}^{2}+2y}+2{y}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{2}+2y} \\  & =2y(y+1){e}^{{x}^{2}+2y}\end{aligned}
$$

a

e
 y(x+y)ex2+2y

q-80400.problem: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}$ given that $\frac{∂f}{∂y}={y}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(1+3xy).$
q-80400.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{∂f}{∂y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(1+3xy)) \\  & =3{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(1+3xy)+3x{y}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(1+3xy)\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${g}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{x-{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{2xy}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{x-{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{(x-{y}^{2})-x}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{{y}^{2}}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y)+{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{2xy}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}}+(-\frac{{y}^{2}}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{2xy-{y}^{2}}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{y(2x-y)}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find gxy(x,y)+gxx(x,y) given that gx(x,y)=xx−y2.

a
y(2x+y)(x−y2)2
b
2x−y2(x−y2)2
c

y(2x−y)(x−y2)2
e
2x−y(x−y2)2
Submit

EXPLANATION

To find gxy(x,y) we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative gx(x,y) with respect to y:

gxy(x,y)=∂∂y(gx(x,y))=∂∂y(xx−y2)=2xy(x−y2)2

To find gxx(x,y) we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative gx(x,y) with respect to x:

gxx(x,y)=∂∂x(gx(x,y))=∂∂x(xx−y2)=(x−y2)−x(x−y2)2=−y2(x−y2)2

Therefore, we have gxy(x,y)+gxx(x,y)=2xy(x−y2)2+(−y2(x−y2)2)=2xy−y2(x−y2)2=y(2x−y)(x−y2)2.

Calculate gxxy(x,y) given that g(x,y)=(x2+y)sin⁡(y2).

gx(x,y)=∂∂x((x2+y)sin⁡(y2))=2xsin⁡(y2)

Next, we find gx(x,y) by differentiating gx(x,y) with respect to x:

gxx(x,y)=∂∂x(gx(x,y))=∂∂x(2xsin⁡(y2))=2sin⁡(y2)

Finally, we find gxxy(x,y) by differentiating gxx(x,y) with respect to y:

gxxy(x,y)=∂∂y(gxx(x,y))=∂∂y(2sin⁡(y2))=4ycos⁡(y2)

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{yz}{x-2z}) \\  & =-\frac{yz}{(x-2z)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-\frac{yz}{(x-2z)^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{z}{(x-2z)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({f}_{xy}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(-\frac{z}{(x-2z)^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{1\cdot (x-2z)^{2}-z\cdot 2(x-2z)\cdot (-2)}{(x-2z)^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{(x-2z)^{2}+4z(x-2z)}{(x-2z)^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{x-2z+4z}{(x-2z)^{3}} \\  & =-\frac{x+2z}{(x-2z)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ at $(1,1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(1,1,1) & =-\frac{1+2\cdot 1}{(1-2\cdot 1)^{3}}=3\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡y\cdot (-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}

$$

$$

fyx(x,y)=∂∂x(fy(x,y))=∂∂x(cos⁡x2cos⁡y)=cos⁡y⋅(−2xsin⁡x2)=−2xsin⁡x2cos⁡y

Finally, we find fyxx(x,y) by differentiating fyx(x,y) with respect to x:

fyxx(x,y)=∂∂x(fyx(x,y))=∂∂x(−2xsin⁡x2cos⁡y)=cos⁡y⋅(−2sin⁡x2−4x2cos⁡x2)=−2cos⁡y(sin⁡x2+2x2cos⁡x2)

$$

2e2x+12ln⁡y

2ye2x

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find the first-order derivative fx(x,y):

fx(x,y)=∂∂x(ye2x+ln⁡y)=2ye2x

Next, we find fxy(x,y) by differentiating fx(x,y) with respect to y:

fxy(x,y)=∂∂y(fx(x,y))=∂∂y(2ye2x)=2e2x

Finally, we find fxyx(x,y) by differentiating fxy(x,y) with respect to x:

fxyx(x,y)=∂∂x(fxy(x,y))=∂∂x(2e2x)=4e2x

First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{z}(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{z}{x+z}) \\  & =\frac{x}{(x+z)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{zx}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{z}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zx}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{z}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{(x+z)^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{(x+z)^{2}-2x(x+z)}{(x+z)^{4}} \\  & =\frac{z-x}{(x+z)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{zxx}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{zx}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zxx}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{zy}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{z-x}{(x+z)^{3}}) \\  & =\frac{-(x+z)^{3}-3(z-x)(x+z)^{2}}{(x+z)^{6}} \\  & =\frac{2(x-2z)}{(x+z)^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate ${f}_{zxx}(x,y,z)$ at $(1,0,1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zxx}(1,0,1) & =\frac{2(1-2(1))}{(1+1)^{4}}=\frac{-2}{16}=-\frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we find the first-order derivative fz(x,y,z):

fz(x,y,z)=∂∂z(zx+z)=x(x+z)2

Now, we find fzx(x,y,z) by differentiating fz(x,y,z) with respect to x:

fzx(x,y,z)=∂∂x(fz(x,y,z))=∂∂x(x(x+z)2)=(x+z)2−2x(x+z)(x+z)4=z−x(x+z)3

Next, we find fzxx(x,y,z) by differentiating fzx(x,y,z) with respect to x:

fzxx(x,y,z)=∂∂x(fzy(x,y,z))=∂∂x(z−x(x+z)3)=−(x+z)3−3(z−x)(x+z)2(x+z)6=2(x−2z)(x+z)4

Finally, we evaluate fzxx(x,y,z) at (1,0,1):

fzxx(1,0,1)=2(1−2(1))(1+1)4=−216=−18
